intro: Videos promising "unlimited free AI" usually mean a shady workaround that breaks the tools' terms and can get your account banned. There's a better way: the official free tiers and model hubs. Here's where to go and what you get.

free.title: Step 1: Use the official free tiers
free.body: Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini all have free plans with daily limits. Use all three: when one runs out, switch to another. Check each one's current limits on its pricing page.

free.title: Step 2: Google AI Studio
free.body: Google AI Studio gives free access to Gemini models for testing and building, with rate limits. Good for trying long documents and images.

free.title: Step 3: Model hubs
free.body: Hubs such as OpenRouter let you use many models from one account, and some models are free with limits. Read each model's terms and don't send private customer data to models you don't know.

free.title: Step 4: Run open models yourself
free.body: Apps like Ollama or LM Studio run open models on your own computer for free. They're slower and less capable than the top models, but private and unlimited.

free.title: Step 5: When paying is worth it
free.body:
Copy this inHere's what I use AI for each week: [tasks], about [hours] hours. Compare doing it on free tiers versus a paid plan of Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini: what limits would I hit, and how much time would a paid plan save? Recommend one.

Avoid any "free unlimited" tool that asks for your login to another AI service.
